birth.stop: Yara: born on the ninth of December
birth.date_confidence: Birth date 9 December 1940 is attested by English Wikipedia and by the 2023 Havana candidate profile. Yara as birthplace is given by Wikipedia and by municipal sources; the National Assembly's own profile page instead gives San Miguel del Padrón, Havana, which is her present electoral district. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved. Coordinate corrected to the town of Yara, Granma, at 20 degrees 16 minutes 36 seconds north, 76 degrees 56 minutes 49 seconds west; the figure carried in the research pool sat about 14 km out in farmland.

stops.stop: Sierra Maestra: received into Column One

stops.date_confidence: The mission is attested and multiply reported; the paperwork is not. stops.stop: Las Vegas de Jibacoa: the armband she will not take off
stops.date_confidence: The destination is attested by Cubainformación's account of her testimony: the enemy camp at Las Vegas de Jibacoa, a consejo popular of Bartolomé Masó municipality in the Yara river valley. Coordinate is approximate to the consejo popular, not landmark-precise.

stops.stop: Las Vegas de Jibacoa: two hundred and fifty-seven handed over
stops.date_confidence: Attested. Cubainformación's account gives the handover on 23 July 1958, with International Committee of the Red Cross delegates René Jecquier and Pierre Schoenholzer receiving 257 prisoners, 23 of them wounded. The dossier's earlier vaguer formula, 'more than two hundred,' is superseded by that figure. Puebla's personal presence at the handover itself, as distinct from the previous day's negotiation, is not separately documented.

stops.stop: Cerro Pelado: the Sherman and the three days
stops.date_confidence: Date attested: Friday 27 September 1958, a three-day action about four kilometres from the Estrada Palma mill, today Bartolomé Masó. The casualty figure was corrected by the verification pass: La Demajagua names five rebel bajas, casualties rather than deaths, among them lieutenants Raúl Verdecia and Luis Arturo Vázquez Matalobos and combatants Miguel López, René Ibarra and Juan Sardiñas Labrada, against 67 enemy dead and wounded. That no Mariana was hurt is Puebla's own claim; at least one account has the platoon's jefa wounded in the opening moments. Coordinate approximates the Estrada Palma area; the hill has no landmark-precise public figure.

stops.stop: Santiago de Cuba: Hero of the Republic of Cuba
stops.date_confidence: The date is attested across EcuRed, Wikipedia and search-corroborated sources: the title Hero of the Republic of Cuba, with the Order of Playa Girón, conferred by Fidel Castro on 2 December 2001. Two corrections apply. The occasion was the 45th anniversary of the Granma landing and FAR Day, not the 40th anniversary of the FAR as first written. And no source reached places the decoration ceremony in Havana; Granma's edition of 2 December 2001 reports the national military review for the 45th anniversary at the Plaza Antonio Maceo in Santiago de Cuba, where Castro spoke, which is why the coordinate is Santiago. Her presence in either city on the day remains undocumented and this placement is a judgement call.

stops.stop: Havana: the interviews that became Marianas en combate
stops.date_confidence: Attested. The interviews underlying the book were conducted with her in Havana on 18 November 2000 and 1 March 2002. Pathfinder Press published the Spanish edition as Marianas en combate, 119 pages, ISBN 978-0-87348-963-8, and the English as Marianas in Combat, 115 pages, ISBN 978-0-87348-957-7, with an introduction by Mary-Alice Waters and a foreword by Juan Almeida Bosque; a Farsi edition followed, ISBN 964-7703-19-8. The publication happened in New York and is cited here rather than staged as her own stop, since she did not travel to it.

stops.stop: Reparto Kohly: the Premio del Barrio
stops.date_confidence: Attested and upgraded by the verification pass. The award of the CDR's Premio del Barrio, in Zona 10 of the Consejo Popular Ceiba-Kohly in Playa municipality, on the CDR's 65th anniversary, is independently reported by Radio Rebelde on 23 September 2025 and by ACN, not only by the municipal notice the first pass could not refetch. The coordinate is corrected to Reparto Kohly at approximately 23.109, -82.411; the two research lenses had given two different and mutually inconsistent figures for the same event.

stops.stop: Havana: eighty-five
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. A public congratulation from the Revolutionary Armed Forces on her eighty-fifth birthday is referenced by ACN under the headline 'Felicitan Fuerzas Armadas a Tete Puebla en su 85 cumpleanos,' found by search but not fetched in full by either pass. Her continuing status as a sitting deputy, reserve brigadier general and ACRC vice president is attested by the Assembly's current profile. The date of her elevation to the ACRC vice presidency is not given anywhere reached, and the Association was founded on 7 December 1993, not 1991 as the dossier first stated.
